title: Response Shape Guide — onboarding tiles & inline hints
creator: Naomi Patel
description: Design a compact, example-driven onboarding flow that teaches users how to author and validate "response shapes" for the Redwood API. Deliver a set of tiled quickstart assets, inline validation visuals, and 1–2 production screenshots for release notes. Focus on clarity for engineers who need to return typed JSON-like objects from models (arrays, optional fields, enums, and nested objects).
acceptance_criteria: Three responsive onboarding tiles that demonstrate: valid response, common error (missing required field), and suggested auto-fix
Inline validation UI mocks: error state, warning state, and suggestion panel showing a diff and example input
Two annotated product screenshots (web console) with callouts for 'Example responses' and 'Validate & lint' buttons
Figma file with component tokens and copy variations for i18n review
Handoff-ready art assets (SVG + PNG) and a short microcopy playbook for engineers and docs writers
comments: 2026-03-09 Naomi Patel: Kickoff — goal is to reduce first-run validation errors by showing example outputs and quick fixes. Prefer compact tiles for minimal cognitive load.
2026-03-10 Marco Alvarez: Exploratory sketches posted in Figma. Experimented with inline suggestion chips and an expandable diff panel.
2026-03-11 Liam Chen (PM): Preference for showing both 'model response' and 'expected contract' side-by-side. Wants automated suggestion toggle in the UI.
2026-03-12 Design review: Chose green micro-check icon for valid responses, amber chevron for warnings, and a subtle red outline for errors. Avoid heavy modal usage.
2026-03-13 Marco Alvarez: Updated mockups pushed; need final copy from docs before handoff. Assigned ENG-2987 for validator API contract.
2026-03-13 Naomi Patel: Added acceptance criteria and initial release note screenshots. Noted accessibility check (color contrast) required before sign-off.
decisions: Use a compact three-tile pattern on the first-run modal rather than a long vertical walkthrough
Inline validator will show the first error with a suggested one-click transform (non-destructive) and a preview
Display paired examples: raw model output on the left, expected response shape on the right (collapsed on mobile)
Microcopy should use active verbs and concrete examples (e.g., 'Add "email" as string')
next_steps: Finalize copy for tiles and suggestion panel (owner: Docs)
Design to produce PNG/SVG exports for release notes and product docs
Engineering to expose 'lint suggestions' endpoint (ENG-2987) and return a suggested patch payload
Accessibility pass: color contrast and screen reader labels
Schedule final review with PM and Research (2026-03-17)
notes: Aim for artifacts that can be dropped into docs and the console release banner. Keep copy concise for engineers skimming onboarding. Avoid introducing new jargon — prefer 'response shape' over 'schema' in microcopy to reduce cognitive overhead. Ensure examples cover arrays and optional fields.
implementation_risks: Backend validator API may return ambiguous suggestions for nested objects
Mobile layout might require collapsing example pairs, which could hide important info
Localization increases microcopy surface area before release
